findings: Today neither slider had the answer near the middle. On each question one slider put the answer about 63% along and the other about 37% (on Abbey Road, 37% and 65%). On Thursday, B had put it near the middle.

Guesses still drift to the slider's middle. On five of the six sliders the median guess sat between the answer and the middle. It was strongest on Abbey Road with slider A (median 12,000 km against 7,027) and on the basketball court with slider B (40 m against 28).

Read with Thursday, where the answer sits is what matters. When B put the answer nearer the middle, B scored clearly higher. With the answer equally far from the middle on both, the two came out close.
caveats: Only three of today's five questions had a slider B. Egypt and the Hillary question gave everyone slider A, so they're left out.
Width changed too. B was narrower than A on the Hagia Sophia and the court and a little wider on Abbey Road, so today doesn't separate width from where the answer sits.
